source: Bailey 1908 general preface, printed iv–v, PDF 14–15
visual_review: Original PDF 15 viewed at 350 dpi; PDF text used only to locate the explanation.
claims: A doubly curved line above a vowel represents nasal n.
Breve i represents a sound intermediate between i and ī.
Contrastively italic u in roman words, or upright u in italic words, represents intermediate u/ū.
Contrastively styled eu denotes the shortened French-type eu vowel; continuous-bar e͞u denotes long eu, distinct from separately marked ēū.
Contrastively styled ai represents shortened ai; the ordinary diphthong is described using English man and aisle.
Underlined sh and zh represent the fricatives contrasted with separately pronounced plain s+h and z+h.
policy: Preserve source graphemes, continuous-bar distinction and both underlined letters. Record contrastive type spans and the author's explanation in per-answer Notes and audit, following the established Kiunthali package. Do not fabricate IPA.
